entities.summary:
The Implementation Force was a multinational peacekeeping deployment to Bosnia and Herzegovina led by NATO in the 1990s, marking a significant shift in global conflict resolution and international cooperation.

This event occurred between 1995 and 1996, involving over 60,000 troops from 37 countries, with a primary goal of enforcing the Dayton Peace Accords and stabilizing the region.

The Implementation Force's success laid the groundwork for future international peacekeeping missions and contributed to the development of more robust and effective global conflict resolution mechanisms.

The legacy of the Implementation Force can be seen in the continued use of international peacekeeping forces in modern conflicts, such as in the Middle East and Africa, and its impact on the development of modern international relations and global governance.

As the former Secretary-General of the United Nations, Boutros Boutros-Ghali, said, "The Implementation Force's success marked a new era in international cooperation and peacekeeping, demonstrating that the international community could come together to address even the most complex and intractable conflicts."
